question: Does the DENR-BMB mainland Luzon inland-wetlands atlas independently list Tagkawayan River in Quezon and provide enough detail to delineate its channel or support fish records?
purpose: Cross-check the source-named Tagkawayan River lead using an official national wetland inventory while preserving the limits of tabular grid/outflow metadata.

sourceReview.publisher: Biodiversity Management Bureau, Department of Environment and Natural Resources
sourceReview.title: Atlas of Inland Wetlands in Mainland Luzon, Philippines
sourceReview.table: Table 2, list of rivers and river systems with map grid, region, province, and outflow
sourceReview.access: PDF text view checked on 2026-11-01; Tagkawayan River row reviewed; text search for Sakang River returned no match. No local copy or map image retained.
sourceReview.reuseTerms: BMB copyright page permits reproduction for educational or non-profit purposes with acknowledgement; it is not an open license and does not grant commercial use. Bangwit public reuse remains unapproved.

findings.tagkawayanRiver: The atlas lists Tagkawayan River in grid P-27, Region IV-A, Quezon, with Ragay Gulf as outflow. This independently supports the source-named feature and a broad outflow association only.
findings.sakangRiver: A text search of the atlas returned no Sakang River match. Because this is a bounded text search, it does not establish that Sakang is absent from the atlas or from the landscape.
findings.geometry: Grid P-27 is an atlas map-grid index, not a coordinate, channel trace, or boundary. The table does not resolve the channel route, reach, confluence, or exact outflow location; no geometry is inferred.
findings.fishEvidence: The river inventory row contains no fish taxa, collection dates, sampling stations, survey methods, vouchers, or fish-presence evidence. No site-specific fish source was retrieved in this cross-check.
findings.salinityAndSafety: The source does not classify salinity, water quality, current flow, fishing access, legal rules, or safety conditions.

nextAction: Obtain a current official hydrography layer or authorized large-scale map before resolving the river route; seek dated, station-resolved fish records with taxonomic and reuse metadata. Keep Sakang and Tagkawayan River separate until an authoritative route/crosswalk resolves their relationship.

sources.supports: DENR-BMB Table 2 lists Tagkawayan River at grid P-27 in Region IV-A, Quezon, with Ragay Gulf as outflow; its BMB reproduction terms are educational/non-profit with attribution.
